In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: if we have a family of objects, and a property that can be checked in polynomial time, then can we find an object in the family that has this property?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the following properties interpolate over a wide range of classes: (i) the property of being the edge set of a graph, hypergraph or matroid; (ii) the property of containing a cycle, cocycle or circuit, respectively, in a graph, hypergraphs or matroid; and (iii) the property of having an edge or hyperedge of some specified order.

if a property is hereditary or cohereditary then it is possible to find a family of sets for which the property is not monotone but for which it is possible to interpolate the property over this family.

if P and Q are, respectively, hereditarily and coheredently well-behaved, then for any graph G with vertex set S, the number of P -subgraphs and the number of Q -subhypergraphs in G are both interpolated by the number of Q and P subgraphs in G.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
if a graph property P is preserved under the operation of taking minors, then the property of not containing any graph with a given minor Q can be tested in polynomial time.

the following properties are interpolative: hereditary and co-heterogenous properties of graphs, hereditary and non-hereditary properties of hypergraphs, hereditary and hereditary/heterogenous properties of matroids, hereditary and antiheterogenous properties of posets, hereditary and homogenous properties of poset extensions, homogenous and homogenous/heterogenous properties for posets and matroids, and hereditary and non-co-hereditary properties for matroids.

if a graph property P on a graph family F is hereditary and a co-graph property Q on a co-graph family F ′ is cohereditary and P and Q are not both trivial, then the function that counts the number of P -graphs on a graph with n vertices and the number of Q -co-graphs on a graph with the same number of vertices interpolates over the set of graphs in F × F ′.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of the aforementioned families, the interpolation properties of a hereditary property are closely related to those of its complementary cohereditary property.
the interpolation properties of a hereditary or a cohereditary property are closely connected to the existence of certain extremal objects.
the interpolation results for graphs and matroids follow from the interpolation results for hypergraphs.
